title: Request Signalboard: unified error taxonomy ribbon + retry walkthrough
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Introduce a new Request Signalboard surface in the Redwood Console that helps engineers quickly triage failed requests by combining an error-taxonomy ribbon, time-series signal lanes (latency, token anomalies, quota hits), and a guided retry walkthrough with payload snapshotting. Goal: reduce mean time-to-diagnose for transient failures and make retry decisions explicit in the Console UX.
acceptance_criteria: Signalboard mock contains: taxonomy ribbon, 3 signal lanes, request list filter by taxonomy tag, and selected-request detail pane
Selected request detail supports: raw payload snapshot, parsed fields view, KV cache state summary, and suggested retry action with parameter presets
Retry walkthrough prototype allows simulating up to 3 retry strategies (linear/backoff/concurrent) and surfaces expected latency/cost impact
Design handoff includes annotated Figma screens, interaction specs, and a redaction policy for PII within payload snapshots
Usability test (n=6 engineers) with tasks measuring time-to-identify root cause shows >=20% improvement vs baseline prototype
decisions: Adopt ‘Signalboard’ as the canonical name (ribbon + lanes) to avoid confusion with existing Debug Panel
Taxonomy will be hierarchical (Error class -> Subclass -> Symptom) and appear as chips in the ribbon for quick filtering
Show a sampled raw payload snapshot by default; provide a one-click expand to full raw with explicit redaction warnings
Retry simulation runs client-side deterministic emulation using recorded timings and kernel profiles to estimate latency/cost
Keep the initial Signalboard read-only for non-admin roles; write actions (trigger retry) gated behind RBAC role 'operator'
tradeoffs: Including full raw payloads increases debugging fidelity but raises PII risk; we mitigate with default redaction plus audit logging
Simulating retries client-side gives fast feedback but is an estimate — we will mark confidence and show aggregated historical results when available
A ribbon-first UX is compact but pushes detail to the pane; this favors engineers comfortable with drilldown and may increase initial discoverability cost
